record.original_question: Consider a torus T 2 bundle over S. Under what hypothesis on the monodromy ρ can we find a foliation with no compact leaves close to a fiber?

evidence.quote: Question 4.4. Consider a torus T 2 bundle over S. Under what hypothesis on the monodromy ρ can we find a foliation with no compact leaves close to a fiber?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed orientable surface and let $E \to S$ be a smooth fiber bundle whose fiber is the $2$-torus $T^2$, classified up to isomorphism by its monodromy representation
$$\rho : \pi_1(S) \longrightarrow \mathrm{MCG}(T^2) \cong \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z}).$$
Inside $E$, the fibers form a codimension-$2$ foliation by tori. One says that a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $E$ exists "close to a fiber" if there is a foliation of $E$ (of codimension $2$) which agrees with the fiber foliation outside an arbitrarily small tubular neighborhood of one fixed fiber $F_0 \subset E$ and is obtained by a perturbation supported in that neighborhood.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the monodromy representation $\rho$ under which the torus bundle $E \to S$ admits, close to a fiber in the sense above, a (codimension-$2$) foliation having no compact leaves.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is phrased as an open research question asking for hypotheses on the monodromy of a $T^2$-bundle over a surface that allow perturbation of the fibration into a foliation without compact leaves near a fiber. A web search produced general background on foliations of torus bundles (Kronecker foliations, flat $T^k$-bundles, punctured torus bundle foliations) but no source resolving this specific perturbation question, so its current status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Foliations of some 3-manifolds which fiber over the circle
status_evidence.snippet: Every hyperbolic three-manifold which is a punctured torus bundle over the circle admits a one-dimensional foliation without closed leaves.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist for foliations without compact leaves on torus bundles, but no source addresses the perturbation question for general $T^2$-bundles over a surface.

status_evidence.title: Monodromy of torus fiber bundles and decomposability problem
status_evidence.snippet: Monodromy of torus fiber bundles and decomposability problem.
status_evidence.claim: Monodromy of $T^2$-bundles is an active topic, but this reference does not resolve the perturbation existence question.
